articles.title: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered Dev Says GTA 6 Was 'Never Part of Our Thinking' When Choosing a Release Date
articles.summary: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered will take on GTA 6 when both games launch this November, but the team behind the arena fighter said Rockstar's latest was "never part of our thinking" when choosing a release date.
articles.body:
Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered will take on Grand Theft Auto 6 when both games launch this November, but the team behind the arena fighter said Rockstar's latest title was "never part of our thinking" when choosing a release date.

In case you haven't heard, GTA 6 comes out November 19, a choice that prompted a wave of other publishers to do everything they can to not launch their games anywhere near that date. The belief is the fallout from a game 13 years in the making will consume the weeks before and after its release, but Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered has emerged as one of the very, very few titles willing to brave the storm.

GTA 6 is indeed primed for an explosive launch , but the team at developer Pipeworks and publisher Atari haven't seemed too worried about how this could affect the remaster for a 2000s classic . In fact, after revealing their November 3 release date , the internet rallied behind the kaiju fighting game, filling feeds with memes as the King of the Monsters (and the upcoming Barbie Rewind ) stomped forward.

As part of a sweeping interview about the new remaster, IGN asked longtime Pipeworks developer and senior designer Simon Strange about how the release date for Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered was chosen and how GTA 6 played a factor in that decision. You might be surprised to hear Rockstar's return to Vice City wasn't really on their radar.

"I have also loved all those memes. I think that's great. Honestly, wasn't even in our heads at all when we were picking the release date," Strange said when asked about how the date was picked. "That's not my business. I make the video games. I'm not too worried about when they come out. If Atari had come to us and said, 'Wow, we can't because we think it's going to affect the sales with GTA,' we would've had that discussion. But no one ever said anything."

Strange made a good point: November 3 is Godzilla's birthday. The original film released on that day in 1954, it's when IP owner Toho recognizes as 'Godzilla Day,' and this year, regardless of whatever is going on with GTA 6, it's when Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is coming to PC and consoles.

Strange clarified that making sure Gojira kept his November birthday was simply a matter of respect. After Pipeworks landed its contract with Atari and pinned a timeline for physical disc manufacturing, the date was locked in.

"So, the GTA thing, that's hilarious," Strange continued. "It's a really cute meme. We've all really enjoyed that. It was never part of our thinking. I wasn't looking at that calendar and being worried in any way, or thinking about what other games are coming out because the Godzilla fans are very excited for it. They'd buy it on any day that it came out, and putting it on Godzilla's birthday, that's just respectful."

Atari admitted it was "certainly aware of the proximity" to the release of GTA 6 when running the numbers tied to its release date. Though still in November, the publisher felt the break between releases gave Godzilla – and Barbie – more than enough room to breathe.

"There were a number of factors at play that led to the selection of November 12 as the release date for Barbie Rewind," an Atari spokesperson told IGN. "In the end, it made the most sense in our calendar, and we felt the cozy/retro vibe of Rewind and the Barbie brand was going to pull in its own, discrete audience.

"It has been exciting to see fans' reactions to the idea of our two games, Godzilla: DAMM Remastered and Barbie Rewind, releasing in November with GTA. The amount and quality of creative content fans are posting online is astounding and a joy to watch. They have made the proximity of the releases a fun event."

Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered Screenshots

GTA 6 or not, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered will launch for PC via Steam, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S November 3. Barbie Rewind will follow November 12, 2026, for PC via Steam, Switch and Switch 2, PS4, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S. Pipeworks is also scheduled to release a PC demo for its Godzilla game October 15.

We'll have more to share from our talk with Pipeworks soon, so be sure to keep an eye out for the full interview. In the meantime, don't forget to check out our preview .

articles.title: Sony CEO Explains Why It Isn’t 'Aggressively Marketing' the PlayStation 5 Anymore
articles.summary: Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki confirmed that the company is no longer “aggressively marketing” the PlayStation 5, saying it’s not necessary now that the console is in the later stages of its life cycle.
articles.body:
Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki confirmed that the company is no longer “aggressively marketing” the PlayStation 5, saying it’s not necessary now that the console is in the later stages of its life cycle.

It’s been nearly six years since the PlayStation 5 first released in November 2020. We’ve come a long way from the days of scalpers making purchases nearly impossible; but these consoles are now largely out of stock at several major retailers once again following Rockstar’s extended look at GTA 6 that released on Netflix this past Thursday.

This marks a sharp turn for the console after it experienced its lowest May sales in the PS5’s history after Sony announced price hikes across all versions of the hardware in April 2026. While highly-anticipated games like GTA 6 seem to be doing all the marketing on Sony’s behalf right now, the company has confirmed that it isn’t fussed about advertising the PlayStation 5 these days.

Hiroki Totoki, CEO at Sony, explained this strategy during an interview with the Wall Street Journal in mid-August, where he admitted that the business’s current goal is profiting off of its existing PlayStation Plus userbase as much as possible.

“We are in the latter half of the life cycle for a PlayStation console,” he said. “That means that we do not need to ‘aggressively sell’ the console today. And rather than that, we’re focusing on recurring revenue from the recurrent userbase. And already, PlayStation Plus has more than 125 million monthly active users today, and how to monetize from those users is quite important for us.”

As expected, comments beneath the video are making sure to point out the company’s future plans to end the production of physical game discs starting January 2028, with one writing on YouTube, “Bring back ‘Only on PlayStation,’ keep physical media.”

“They’ll regret terminating physical media,” another said.

“Maybe they can revert and bring back physical discs, for starters,” another wrote.

These comments are the same under any major post discussing PlayStation, or even posts from the brand, itself. Advertisements for film adaptations of popular games on its consoles are facing a similar fate as players inundate the comments section protesting Sony’s plans for an all-digital future — a future that’s looking increasingly bleak, based on the company’s recent statements to disgruntled customers.

In July, Sony’s chief financial officer, Lin Tao, confirmed that it will "cautiously move forward" with killing off physical discs, arguing that this decision was made in response to the increasing “digitization of contents.”

And on August 21, Sony responded to a class action lawsuit from consumers who argued that the PlayStation digital store doesn’t make it obvious that players are merely purchasing a revocable license, instead of fully owning the games permanently.

“In the digital age, it is not plausible to allege that reasonable consumers believed they were obtaining ‘ownership’ of a digital game,” the company said.

Thus far, the future of the PlayStation 6 is unknown, but players are worried that both this console and Xbox's Project Helix will be digital-only by default.

articles.title: Fans Can't Decide if Hideo Kojima Actually Liked Ridley Scott's The Dog Stars
articles.summary: Kojima’s brief review for Ridley Scott’s latest movie betrays how he really feels about the divisive post-apocalyptic flick… At least, that’s what fans are saying.
articles.body:
Hideo Kojima’s brief review for Ridley Scott’s The Dog Stars betrays how he really feels about the divisive post-apocalyptic flick… At least, that’s what fans are saying.

Scott’s latest movie hasn’t exactly been well-received. The movie was a box office bomb, earning just $19 million during its global opening. Critics’ opinions have been similarly brutal, with IGN’s Leanne Butkovic scoring the film a 5 out of 10 , calling it a "post-apocalyptic survival story that’s encased in three layers of emotionally protective bubble wrap with a wild third-act twist."

Fans believe Kojima, an acclaimed video game director and film connoisseur, feels much the same way, owing to a trend they’ve observed in his social media posts discussing movies he’s recently watched. If you’re familiar with Kojima’s online presence, you’ll know that the man isn’t very fussed about public perception (some of his retweets are straight up WILD ), but when it comes to expressing his dislike for films, fans claim that he often doesn’t say anything of substance at all.

Usually, when Kojima likes a movie, he’ll create a lengthy post diving into everything he admired about it, as seen in the high praise he gave to Kane Parson’s Backrooms . However, for The Dog Stars, he merely remarked on what he initially expected from the film… and that’s about it.

"Peter Heller's original novel, The Dog Stars (previously published in Japanese under the title Itsuka Boku ga Kaeru Basho / The Place I'll Return to Someday), has been sitting on my bookshelf for years, unread. Since it's literary fiction rather than science fiction, I went to see the movie, picturing it might be something along the lines of Cormac McCarthy's The Road. The music was by Harry. They weren't selling (didn’t make) a pamphlet for the film," he said on his English X account.

It was a strikingly bland post in comparison to his other, far more colorful reviews of films he distinctly loves — and because of this, fans are convinced that Kojima, much like other reviewers, wasn't its biggest fan. Though of course, we can’t outright say that, given he didn’t say as much in his post.

"You can tell he didn’t like it because he said nothing about the actual film, lol," one user said in the comments.

"He said nothing about the film so he hated it lmao," another joked.

"Ridley's a genius, he created a genre of Kojima tweets. Saying nothing about the actual film while talking about it," yet another said.

Scott’s name has been all over social media as of late, in part due to The Dog Stars as well as several interviews he’s given to the press. In one of these interviews, Scott confirmed that he is developing a sequel to Alien: Covenant with Michael Fassbender, partly because he believes the Alien franchise he created "needs some help," as he felt Alien: Romulus was just "OK."

articles.title: 'It Ended My Old Life'  — DayZ Felt Like Dying, Says Creator
articles.summary: Dean Hall, creator of zombie survival game DayZ and founder of RocketWerkz, seems to have a complicated relationship with his biggest hit, which was first released as a mod for Arma 2 in 2012.
articles.body:
Dean Hall, creator of zombie survival game DayZ and founder of RocketWerkz, seems to have a complicated relationship with his biggest hit, which was first released as a mod for Arma 2 in 2012.

"When DayZ happened, it was like dying," Hall told PC Gamer . "It ended my old life. My relationship with everyone who I knew up to that point changed completely."

"It was obviously an amazing thing that happened to me," he added. "I loved making the mod, and I loved that feeling, and I've been chasing it ever since."

The game started life as a mod for Arma 2 and its expansion pack Operation Arrowhead and was so popular with gamers that just a few months later Hall announced that Arma 2 developer Bohemia Interactive was creating a standalone version of the game , with Hall as project lead.

"People think I'm a game developer who came up from [being] a modder, and I would say I'm a modder who makes games during the day," Hall added. "I was born a modder, and I will die a modder. And I think if there's a lesson out there for any aspiring game devs, I think it's mod games. You will learn even faster than making them."

In February 2014 Hall stepped down from the project lead role and went on to start his own studio, RocketWerkz. Its releases since include VR strategy game Out Of Ammo and space survival sim Icarus and is currently working on Kitten Space Agency. As well as being a spaceflight sim, the game is a proof of concept for Hall's contribution-based development model.

"With Kitten Space Agency, the game is completely free," he said. "It's funded entirely by contributions. So that really puts it in front of the gamer's face. If you want this game to exist, how much is it worth? Because it's all on you."

articles.title: Lion King Lyricist Ordered to Pay Nearly $40,000 to Cover Comedian's Attorney Fees After Suing Him Over Joke Translation of 'Circle of Life' Lyrics
articles.summary: The Grammy-winning lyricist behind The Lion King’s famous opening vocals is now being ordered to pay nearly $40,000 in attorneys’ fees after unsuccessfully suing a comedian for poking fun at the song.
articles.body:
The Grammy-winning lyricist behind The Lion King’s famous opening vocals is now being ordered to pay nearly $40,000 in attorneys’ fees after unsuccessfully suing a comedian for poking fun at the song.

South African comedian Learnmore Mwanyenyeka, better known by his alias Jonasi, was hit with a $27 million lawsuit in March 2026 from plaintiff Lebohang Morake, who penned the Zulu lyrics that are sung at the beginning of "The Circle of Life" in Disney’s animated animal epic.

Jonasi made the joke during an episode of the One54 Africa podcast in February, where he playfully translated the line as, “Look, there is a lion! Oh my god.” While it got a laugh from the show’s hosts at the time, the song’s lyricist didn’t find it very funny.

A March 16 lawsuit filed in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California labeled Jonasi’s humorous mistranslation as a “fabricated, trivializing distortion meant as a sick joke,” saying it damaged the “royal praise poetry” written by Morake that "stands independently as an African vocal proclamation grounded in South African tradition” outside of its use in The Lion King.

For reference, Morake’s lawsuit translated the line “Nants’ingonyama bagithi Baba” as “All hail the king, we all bow in the presence of the king.” The suit mentioned that “ngonyama” can also translate to Lion in Zulu, but argued that the term “signifies kingship” due to Praise Imbongi tradition and the use of royal metaphor, per NBC News .

In a now-deleted Instagram post, Jonasi said that he and Morake spoke about the situation privately. "This was just a joke, and comedy always has a way of starting a conversation,” he said. “I told him this. This is now your chance to actually educate people because now people are listening. I was even ready to create a video with him, to be honest. Personally, I had no idea it had a deeper meaning."

Jonasi was famously served a lawsuit over the joke during a live performance that same month. Now, five months later, the suit has been struck down, with Morake ordered to pay thousands of dollars to cover Jonasi’s attorney fees.

More specifically, he’ll have to shell out $39,560, as laid out in a court order filed on August 28, 2026. The order says the “prevailing defendant” ultimately won the case due to an Anti-SLAPP motion, which basically means the court struck down what it believed was a frivolous and costly suit designed to punish Jonasi for his joke.

The suit was officially dismissed on July 10, 2026. Speaking with the Rolling Stone , Jonasi’s lawyer, Bryan Sullivan, celebrated the ruling as a win for free speech.

“We have always believed this was a frivolous lawsuit in violation of our client’s First Amendment rights,” he told the outlet.

For more Lion King news, check out IGN's review of the movie's Diamond Edition Blu-ray version , or take a peek at our take on Mufasa: The Lion King.

articles.title: RIP to Disney+'s Live-Action Gargoyles Reboot
articles.summary: Gargoyles' creator Greg Weisman has revealed that the live-action adaptation of the '90s cartoon series is no longer moving forward.
articles.body:
Gargoyles creator Greg Weisman has revealed that the live-action adaptation of the '90s cartoon series is no longer moving forward. The show had been planned as a Disney+ release, with James Wan's production company, Atomic Monster, leading the project.

"Well, I know the live-action side of it is, uh, the Atomic Monster had the license to develop a live-action Gargoyles for Disney+, and that’s dead," he told ComicsOnline . "I have no idea about animation, but there are no current plans for live-action."

The show first aired in 1994 and centered on a bunch of (you guessed it) Gargoyles, who turn to stone in daylight hours and find themselves in a modern-day New York City, becoming its defenders. The iconic Keith David played the leader of the petrifying pack, Goliath, and his clone, Thailog.

The live-action reboot was announced in 2023 with Annabelle and The Nun writer Gary Dauberman as showrunner, writer, and executive producer. Last year, Dauberman told Collider that the original cartoon "lends itself to a really cool live-action version," and said his take would be "still keeping that darkness to it."

If the news is hard to hear, you can still stream all three seasons of the original Gargoyles animated version on Disney+. In a 2021 IGN retrospective , our writer argued the show "helped to redefine cartoon villainy in the ’90s."

She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

articles.title: GTA 6 Gets Even More New Screenshots as Rockstar Locks in for November Launch
articles.summary: It seems the drought of Grand Theft Auto 6 news has finally come to an end, as Rockstar has published even more screenshots for fans to comb through.
articles.body:
It seems the drought of Grand Theft Auto 6 news has finally come to an end, as Rockstar has published even more screenshots for fans to comb through.

It seems the floodgates for GTA 6's summer marketing campaign have finally opened after last week's extended look gameplay premiere. Today, instead of video for Jason and Lucia's story, Rockstar has published a nice selection of fresh screenshots, revealing new options for character customization, potential story moments, and a closer look at Vice City.

Rockstar has an entire page on its website dedicated to new GTA 6 screenshots that range from pictures of in-progress robberies and explosive cars to muddin' parties and romantic nights out on the town. Of the 99 images available, at least three have never been seen before, and many of the others are only now getting high-quality releases. You can see the three new GTA 6 screenshots, as well as some of the other images Rockstar shared, below.

Grand Theft Auto fans are still parsing through all of the content themselves, but three images in particular seem to be brand new and have fans especially worked up: one of Jason and Lucia in a car, a real-life Miami condo recreated in Vice City, and a menacing shot of the two protagonists as they looked down on someone they maybe, probably just murdered. It's a lot to go through, so let's start with that first one.

Players will probably spend a lot of time in GTA 6, so it's nice to know there will be what seems to be a shopping mall's worth of customization items to dress up Jason and Lucia. The first image puts that on full display, showing the latter criminal decked out with piercings, tattoos, and bangs. Jason, meanwhile, looks almost like a different person thanks to his slick-backed do and facial hair.

Next up is that seaside condo. The average person may look at the two towering buildings and think nothing of them, but Florida residents (and eagle-eyed GTA 6 fans) immediately recognize the spot as a recreation of Miami's Two Tequesta Point . After one fan located the real-life inspiration for Jason and Lucia's apartment , it shouldn't be a surprise to see Rockstar went all out when it came to creating its ideal modern Vice City.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

Then, finally, there's that last image. It, however, raises more questions than answers, seemingly revealing what could be a glimpse from a story mission. Another image of the GTA 6 couple shows them embracing each other as the police close in, but we have some waiting to do before we learn more.

The real news here, though, is that the wait is almost over. The 27-minute extended look has come and gone , Rockstar is reportedly talking with Florida officials about a big marketing rollout , and we've consistently gotten updates for the last few days. X/Twitter user @bb3jc9 also noticed that a GTA 6 pre-order tab recently appeared in GTA Online. More than anything, fans are just happy to see that, after numerous delays and 13 years of waiting, it looks like GTA 6's release date has finally stuck .

"The next 11 weeks are going to be insane (I hope)," one fan said .

The world will be playing GTA 6 when it launches for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, 2026. You can check out IGN's interview and preview here. When Rockstar plans to reveal more about its game is unclear, but we'll be sure to catch and report on every drop shared as they're revealed.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Developers Address Time to Kill Criticisms and Tweak Weapons in New Beta Update
articles.summary: Infinity Ward has addressed the state of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's time to kill and tweaked a handful of weapons in a new beta update.
articles.body:
Infinity Ward has addressed the state of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's time to kill and tweaked a handful of weapons in a new beta update.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's beta is coming to a close, but Infinity Ward is still updating the hell out of it. The latest update was pushed this morning before the beta officially winds down tomorrow. Per the patch notes , a bunch of weapons have been tuned following feedback from fans, including the ISO Nightshade SMG, which got a slight buff with damage improvements. The PPSH, Krait P68, Han 86, and Hyeon Burst all got various buffs as well, with the latter's headshot damage multiplier increasing from 1 to 1.1.

A handful of weapons got nerfed, but the most notable hit was taken by the M4 Hurricane variant, which had its damage decreased. Infinity Ward also used the update as an opportunity to address the game's time to kill, which was divisive in the first beta weekend for being far too fast. Following some adjustments, MW4's TTK is more in line with where Infinity Ward wants it to be.

"Over the weekend, we've been reviewing your gameplay and feedback carefully," said the studio. "We feel that TTK on average is much closer to where we wanted it to be after Weekend 1, but there's always room to refine individual weapons to make sure they're balanced across the board. These changes provide tuning for each class to do well at its role."

Being responsive to feedback is a big part of Infinity Ward's mission this year. Fans were frustrated with Modern Warfare 2 (2022) because it felt like Infinity Ward ignored or brushed off critiques about major aspects such as gameplay pacing, mini-map functionality, and SBMM. With Modern Warfare 4, Infinity Ward is trying to be more receptive.

"I think in MW2, we definitely didn't communicate as well as we should have," said Studio Multiplayer Creative Director Joe Cecot in an exclusive interview with IGN . "I think we've remedied that in crazy ways with this project. Even with the amount of stuff that I get sent to my desk to review like, "Hey, we want to respond to this." And then I review copy or I'm writing something, it's a huge shift. That's going to continue into live support and I think you see it at our studio head level. [Infinity Ward co-studio head] Mark Grigsby is posting, the Infinity Word account is posting, the Call of Duty account is posting, and they're all in unison posting. They're not separate from each other. I think it's really powerful and it feels really good to us."

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: 'Take My Money Now' — Viral Game Lets Your Giant Pet Cat Join You in Combat, and Players Can't Wait
articles.summary: An indie game where players share heartbeats with their pet cat, which can transform into a giant kitty big enough to ride on and defeat enemies, is going viral — and it’s not hard to see why.
articles.body:
An indie game where players share heartbeats with their pet cat, which can transform into a giant kitty big enough to ride on and defeat enemies, is going viral — and it’s not hard to see why.

The game, titled Ylem’s Cat, is the debut offering of a small, independent studio based in Guangzhou, China. It was first revealed at gamescom this year, and it’s already sweeping across social media.

Per its listing on Steam , the game’s official logline is as follows: “Ylem’s Cat is an action-adventure game driven by the bond between a girl and her cat. Led by curiosity and knowledge, Molly sets out on a journey to find her missing mother across a dying planet, exploring ruins and uncovering the truth buried within the giants.”

While the game’s graphics are truly stunning and its gameplay loop seems immersive enough, the cat is the real selling point here. It can join you in combat and bop enemies on the head, and you can even use the reflection from your bow to play with it like a laser pointer. The feline’s realistic behavior will no doubt be a selling point for cat lovers (but we have to warn you that it does seem like it falls into mortal peril at one point in the trailer).

The game follows Molly in the wake of a terrible disaster after a mysterious cat saves her life. The cat — which she names Mio, after its meow — now shares a heartbeat with Molly, and it’s being hunted by robotic beings named Sentinels.

Mio helps you both in combat and in exploration, and can grow bigger or smaller depending on the task at hand. “In combat, the more you learn to fight together, the easier it becomes,” the game’s Steam page reads. “In exploration, keep an eye on Mio — the little cat has its own curiosities, and those might matter more than you think.”

articles.title: The Stormfell Academy Book Series Is a Great New Fantasy Series for Fans of Harry Potter and Mistborn
articles.body:
When I first started reading Torsten Weitze's The Tower of Beggars, I was expecting something similar to the Harry Potter books . What I got instead was an entirely unique story filled with tales of gods and inequality. And while magic is a big part of this world, the first book in the series is true to its name and largely centers around a beggar's perspective. If you're looking for a good new fantasy series to dig into, I highly recommend checking it out.

The Tower of Beggars: Stormfell Academy Book One

The Tower of Beggars follows the story of Niri, a 16 year-old-girl with the kind of heritage that doesn't do her any favors. Her father was an Aeldae and her mother was a human, making her fully hated by any followers of the Crimson God throughout the Splinterlands. The hatred isn't unfounded; after all, the Aeldae had enslaved humans before the fall of their god, but that fact doesn't make Niri's life any easier. With both her parents dead, the story begins with her working as a coal girl for her mysterious nuncle (uncle) Vasdram, who seems to have a serious gambling problem.

The story starts out a bit slow as Niri's life as a coal girl sets up her beggar origins as well as the larger lore around the primary god, Malkar, who sets the rules of the land. It isn't until Niri is forced to leave her home and make use of Vasdram's Beggar Coin that the story truly gets going. Though I could argue that it really starts to become a fun read once Grabbasnack, the gold-eating pocket dragon, is introduced as a character in the first act.

As a protagonist, Niri is quite likable. She's smart, courageous, and tends to make the unselfish choice when it's presented to her. She's kind of the antithesis to the world she lives in, one which praises only selfishness and strength. Her biggest drawback as a character is that she is generally pretty weak and is constantly freezing up due to fear, which she calls "Sinking." If it weren't for the loyal companions she meets along the way, she'd clearly be dead in a hurry.

Overall, the story of The Tower of Beggars: Stormfell Academy Book One is quite good, but it wouldn't be nearly as enjoyable without the addition of the pocket dragon. Gh'rab-ehl-sh'naak (AKA Grabbasnack) is a tiny dragon who exclusively eats gold and can't keep his mouth shut. He's also an incredibly loyal friend and, after being freed from captivity by Niri, he becomes her first true steadfast companion. Thanks to his penchant for saying whatever he thinks at pretty much any moment, he keeps all of the dialogue feeling fresh when it could have run the risk of being too serious or stale. His constant search for gold to nibble on is also delightfully contradictory to the derelict environments Niri often finds herself in.

As for the actual magical school part of the story, it feels pretty light in the first book. While Niri does get admitted to the Stormfell Academy, she quickly finds that the Tower of Beggars isn't exactly a dedicated place of learning. She is only allowed to take a few different classes thanks to her Beggar Coin, but they are mostly designed for preparing lower-class citizens to become fodder for war. And despite free admittance to the academy, most of the folks in the Tower of Beggars are focused on finding riches (or just enough money to survive) in the monster-filled crater just outside of the academy.

The delicate balance between surviving and actually finding time to learn is where this story really shines. Niri has a fire to her, but she's ultimately weak and has the world working against her. Even though she's able to make it into the tower, she quickly finds that her admittance doesn't make her an equal by any means. The same prejudices that plagued her outside of the gates of Stormfell are only amplified by the cutthroat environment of the Tower of Beggars. The Crimson God himself promotes strength above all else, and Niri has to constantly struggle to make choices that will keep her alive without compromising her generous heart.

articles.title: PlayStation Is Set to Pay Out $7.85 Billion to Users as Part of Class-Action Lawsuit
articles.summary: PlayStation users may be eligible for a cut of a $7.85 billion class-action lawsuit settlement very soon.
articles.body:
PlayStation users may be eligible for a cut of a $7.85 billion class-action lawsuit settlement very soon.

The class-action lawsuit, Caccuri v. Sony Interactive Entertainment , alleged that Sony violated anti-trust laws by forcing "consumers to pay more for certain digital games than they otherwise would have paid on the PlayStation Store.” It did so by removing digital vouchers for games from third-party retailers like Amazon or key resellers, meaning if you want a digital copy of a PlayStation game, you must buy it directly from the PlayStation Store.

This move removed the freedom of choice for a lot of players and has only become a hotter topic in recent months, as PlayStation plans to exit the physical media market in 2028. The lawsuit alleges that this decision pushed customers into paying more for games through the PlayStation Store.

Sony denied any wrongdoing and pushed back against claims that members were damaged by its actions. The court also hasn't decided if the company actually violated any laws yet, but it has preliminarily approved a $7.85 billion settlement, subject to a final approval hearing on October 15. That hearing will decide how the funds will be distributed, lock in the final sum, and pay out attorney fees. For further updates, you can check out the official settlement website .

To be eligible for a cut of this settlement, you'll need to be a United States citizen who purchased a game from this list between April 1, 2019 and December 31, 2023. If you are elligible, PlayStation will deposit funds into your PSN account at a later date. If you deactivated your PSN, you can request a cash payment by submitting your qualifying purchase history to this email address: info@PSNDigitalGamesSettlement.com. It's unclear if you can request a cash payment with an existing PSN account, but if you can, PlayStation users can view their purchase history directly through their account on PlayStation's website if needed.

As is the case with class-action lawsuits, we won't know how much money individuals will get until it starts going out. It could be a few bucks, it could be dozens of dollars. Either way, free money is free money.

In related news, a separate lawsuit has seen PlayStation admitting that players don't own their digital games . This may not come as a shock to some, since the terms of service often use the term "license" in relation to digital games, but it is messy optics as the company tries to navigate backlash from its pivot to an all-digital future.

The Switch 2 Pro controller is arguably the best gamepad for the Switch 2 console, but not everyone wants to pay $90 for it. Instead, why not consider the original Switch Pro controller - which has identical build quality and ergonomics and nearly the same feature set - for nearly half the price?

Amazon Relsale is selling used "like new" Nintendo Switch Pro controllers for just $48.12 after an automatic 15% discount is applied during checkout. Amazon Resale is Amazon's official outlet for used items. Amazon states that this "Like New" item "looks and functions as if it were new and comes in original packaging." You still get the 30-day Amazon return policy so it's a much safer option than buying a used controller off Facebook Marketplace.

Nintendo Switch Pro Controller for $48.12

Most importantly, the Switch Pro controller is compatible with the Switch 2. Although the Switch Pro controller supports HD rumble with haptic feedback, the new Switch 2 Pro controller has upgraded "HD Rumble 2".

articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker PC Settings Guide: Maximize Your PC Performance By Tweaking These Options
articles.body:
While 2026 has so far been packed with incredible PC games, The Blood of Dawnwalker was the one that I was looking forward to the most. Not only does it come from a game director with an incredible pedigree, but ever since system requirements were first revealed in February , I knew that this game would absolutely punish my PC – and I’m into that.

Luckily, Rebel Wolves has since lightened the system requirements a bit, now only recommending an RTX 4070 Ti for 4K 60 fps gameplay, rather than the RTX 5090 I thought it was going to require at the beginning of the year. And now that I’ve had a chance to play it, I’m pleasantly surprised at its performance, even if the visuals are a little mixed.

Just like a lot of RPGs of this scope, much of what makes The Blood of Dawnwalker so beautiful is its environments. Just walking through the town and the forest in the opening chapter is jaw-dropping, with realistic foliage and water. The character models don’t quite reach the same fidelity, but I’m ok with that when just walking through the world looks as good as it does.

The Blood of Dawnwalker - Prologue Screenshots

The Blood of Dawnwalker PC Settings Explained

While The Blood of Dawnwalker is available on Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5 , PC is where it truly shines. This game has pretty much every graphics option I’d like in a modern game, and avoids clumping a bunch of graphics techniques into one banner. The game is quite heavy to run maxed out, but there is genuinely enough room to dial it in for better performance, pretty much whichever hardware you’re playing it on.

Keep in mind, though, that The Blood of Dawnwalker is running on Unreal Engine 5. The game handily avoids the kinds of problems that have plagued Star Wars Zero Company and Halo: Campaign Evolved , but it is pretty heavy, especially on your CPU. The game will still run on a handheld, technically, but not particularly well. I played it a bit on the Lenovo Legion Go 2 at the lowest settings at 900p, and got around 24 fps indoors. So, I’d stick to your main tower for this one.

But even on a tower, Blood of Dawnwalker can be very demanding. At 4K with DLSS set to Quality and on the Ultra preset, the RTX 5090 gets anywhere from 70–90 fps before frame generation. It is incredibly smooth, but that’s the type of performance you’d expect from an RTX 5090.

Here's my list of recommended graphics settings, so you can spend less time wondering what each option does and more time living your best vampiric life.

Shadow Quality: This one’s pretty simple and just changes the resolution and accuracy of shadows. This game has a lot of dynamic lighting, though, and this is probably one of the first settings I’d turn down to improve performance. But, it is a game where shadows do add a lot to the atmosphere, so you’ll have to weigh the importance there. Mid-Range PC: High; Handheld: Low

Light Quality: It’s hard to tell from looking at this game’s gorgeous lighting, especially in the mornings and evenings, but there is no ray tracing on offer here. Still, this setting will change how detailed lights are, and the intensity of effects like global illumination and diffuse lighting. Turn it down if your performance is struggling. Mid-Range PC: High; Handheld: Low

Reflections Quality: I’ll admit that I’m only a couple of hours into this absolutely massive RPG, but at least in my time with it, there aren’t that many reflective surfaces. Still, this setting will change how detailed screen space reflections are, so turn it down if you start getting performance drops around water or other reflective surfaces. Mid-Range PC: Medium; Handheld: Low

Post-Processing Quality: You’ll be able to toggle individual post-processing features on or off further down in the settings, so this changes how good all of those effects look. I’d keep this up on higher settings if you like a cinematic aesthetic, but you can effectively turn it off if you don’t really care about bloom or motion blur. Mid-Range PC: High; Handheld: Low

Texture Quality: This mostly affects how much VRAM the game is going to eat up. I’ve spent most of my time in this game with this maxed out, and the game ate up about 10–12GB of VRAM. So I’d stick to Ultra on 16GB plus, High on anything from 8–12GB and medium or low if you have less than 8GB of VRAM. This should be one of the first things you turn down if you start running into stuttering.

Effects Quality: This mostly affects particle effects, and there are surprisingly a lot of them in this game. This is going to be heavier on your CPU than anything, so I’d turn this down if you’re getting bottlenecked there. Mid-Range PC: Ultra; Handheld: Low

Shading Quality: This is just another way to scale the lighting in Blood of Dawnwalker. I’d turn this down early if you’re struggling to hit 60 fps. Mid-Range PC: High; Handheld: Low

Foliage Quality: Simply put, foliage in this game is gorgeous, almost at the same level as something like Assassin’s Creed Shadows. But, if you notice your performance start to tank when you’re running around in the wilderness, you should probably drop this to a lower setting. But, really you should at least try running it a higher setting just to see what it looks like. Mid-Range PC: Medium or High; Handheld: Low

Detail Quality: Maybe it’s just me, but having the option to tweak “Detail Quality” feels a little like changing “Detail Details.” Regardless, this changes a lot of volumetric effects like fog, along with destructible objects. I’d turn this down if you’re running into CPU issues. Mid-Range PC: Medium; Handheld: Low

Volumetric Quality: This setting also changes volumetrics, but focuses more on their resolution. I’ll always turn volumetrics down before anything else, and that doesn’t change in Blood of Dawnwalker. Mid-Range PC: Medium; Handheld: Low

Upscaling Technology: Unlike a lot of other Unreal Engine 5 games, Blood of Dawnwalker doesn’t try and shove TSR down your throat. Instead, Blood of Dawnwalker supports all three major upscalers from GPU manufacturers and the one you should choose depends on which graphics card you’re using. Nvidia users should use DLSS, AMD users should use FSR and Intel users should use XeSS.

Upscaling Mode: Because this game is hard to run, I’d go with upscaling on performance mode if you’re struggling to hit 60 fps. However, keep in mind that performance mode will look pretty rough on lower resolutions, so you might want to lower lighting settings first.

Frame Generation: This uses AI to insert interpolated frames in between rendered frames. This will nearly double your frame rate, but will increase latency by a little bit. But because this isn’t a competitive game, and isn’t even that fast-paced, I’d recommend just turning this on, especially if you have a high-refresh rate gaming monitor.

Motion Blur: This is just a toggle to either enable or disable motion blur. I hate motion blur, you might love it. It’s really up to you. It won’t affect performance all that much either way.

Bloom: This is another toggle, but this time for Bloom. These are the little rays of light that you sometimes see coming off of the sun or something. This will affect performance a bit, so I’d turn it off if you’re playing on a low-end GPU. But for most people on a modern gaming PC, it probably won’t make that much of an impact.

Chromatic Aberration: This is an effect that tries to mimic a camera lens. I don’t notice much of a difference whether its enabled or not, so I’d try it each way and see what you prefer. This won’t affect performance much if at all.

Depth of Field: This will blur distant objects, especially in cutscenes. This is a nice effect, and I usually leave it on, but turn it off if you want everything to be crystal clear.

articles.title: Gal Gadot Says James Gunn and Peter Safran Told Her Wonder Woman 3 Was Happening Before Its Messy Cancellation
articles.summary: Former DC movie star Gal Gadot has opened up about the confusion surrounding Wonder Woman 3, saying that, even though it "wasn't handled elegantly," it's "all good" between her, James Gunn, and Peter Safran.
articles.body:
Former DC movie star Gal Gadot has opened up about the confusion surrounding Wonder Woman 3 , saying that, even though it "wasn't handled elegantly," it's "all good" between her, James Gunn, and Peter Safran.

The story of Wonder Woman 3 is a bit of a mess. Gadot's return was seemingly greenlit , canceled , greenlit again, and, finally, canceled in the early 2020s, with its supposed early days unfortunately weighed down by leadership changes behind the scenes as Gunn and Safran stepped in to take over the DC movie business.

One of the stranger updates during the kerfuffle saw the actress confirm the two superhero film execs had told her she would come back as Diana Prince for Wonder Woman 3 before it was reported that Gunn and Safran didn't have any plans for a third movie from director Patty Jenkins after all. It was a back-and-forth painful enough to watch from the outside, but it was probably even more grueling on the inside.

Gadot recalled the confusion during an interview with Happy, Sad, Confused . She again confirmed that Gunn and Safran assured her Wonder Woman 3 was happening, going as far as to say that there was never a clear moment when the project was formally canned.

"No, they told me the opposite," she answered when asked about the circumstances surrounding the cancellation. "They were like, 'We're going to develop it with you, [Wonder Woman 3], but I saw the way everybody else was handled, right?"

The "everybody else" she referred to involves the former DC movie universe, often called the DC Extended Universe. It comprised films led by Gadot as Wonder Woman, Jason Momoa as Aquaman, and Henry Cavill as Superman. Cavill, in particular, had it rough when Gunn and Safran laid the groundwork for the DCU, as he also officially announced he would reprise his role as Clark Kent in October 2022 just to U-turn two months later .

DCEU Movie Teases That Were Never Paid Off

"The Henry situation was not handled elegantly, to say the least," Gadot added. "Same with Patty – was not handled elegantly. I feel like, you know, we're all adults and it's all good, and it's not even about them."

She continued, saying that Gunn, Safran, and the rest of DC Studios are going "to do what they believe in, and it's all good." She said she's grateful she had the opportunity to be Wonder Woman at all and sends her best to whoever plays the part of the Amazonian superhero next. That said, don't expect her to ever play the part again, even if Gunn and Safran come knocking at her door.

"For me to go and do, for example, another Wonder Woman, I'm not sure I would at this point in my life with four children and different schools, and all of that. To check out all of them for such a long period of time… It doesn't work with my life anymore at this point."

For now, Wonder Woman 3 isn't happening, and it's unclear when the character will make her entrance into the DCU. Next up are movies like Clayface and Man of Tomorrow . Lanterns , one of the comic book movie universe's TV shows, is in the midst of its first season, with The People v. Gorilla Grodd confirmed to be in development. You can see the full breakdown for everything coming to the DCU here .

articles.title: AMC Theaters Launches Its Own Film Distribution Company As Small Budget Movies Soar
articles.summary: AMC Theaters isn’t merely a destination for watching new film releases; it now helps make those releases happen.
articles.body:
AMC Theaters isn’t merely a destination for watching new film releases; it now helps make those releases happen.

Launched on August 31, 2026, AMC has rolled out Leawood Films, its very own movie distribution label that aims to bring small or mid-sized flicks to the big screen that have been completely financed and finished.

Speaking in a press release, AMC Entertainment chairman and CEO Adam Aron cited moviegoers’ increasing appetites for independent films.

“Ultimately, moviegoers consistently demonstrate their appetite for a wide variety of theatrical content, and we believe there are more outstanding films that deserve the opportunity to find audiences on the big screen,” he said. “Through Leawood Films, we believe we can bring meaningful value to filmmakers whose movies might otherwise not get made, or which might not be taken to theatres.

“We can assure them the availability of movie theatre screens and attractive economics, as well as have them benefit from our relationships across the exhibition industry, our proven marketing capabilities, and our extensive experience connecting theatrical content with moviegoing audiences.”

This doesn’t come as a huge surprise; some of the biggest films of the year were created on comparatively measly budgets ( Obsession , Backrooms ), and YouTube star Markiplier’s independent horror flick Iron Lung had so much hype behind it that AMC Theaters, along with several other major cinema chains, picked it up to help the movie become one of biggest independent film releases of all time.

“Leawood Films is being created with a straightforward objective, given that substantial excess capacity exists in the movie theatre industry: to bring more movies to theaters. If we can take steps to ensure that a few extra movies come to theaters each year, it is gravy for AMC in the United States and Odeon in Europe, as well as for our fellow exhibitors,” Aron added.

Tangentially, it’s worth noting that Markiplier also approached YouTube with the idea of distributing independent films on its platform, making AMC the latest major entertainment company to take notes based on shifting audience demands.

As per reporting from Deadline , Leawood Films’ board of advisors is made up of former Warner Bros Group chairman and Toby Emmerich, former Walt Disney Studios marketing president Ricky Strauss and former Paramount distribution veteran Kyle Davies.

AMC says this venture is a “low-risk opportunity” with the potential to catapult the next big film into the limelight. Perhaps Nicole Kidman wasn’t wrong when she said AMC Theaters “make movies better.”

articles.title: The 65" Samsung S90F 4K QD-OLED TV Is Better Than Its 2026 Successor, and It's on Sale for Labor Day
articles.summary: The S90F is the last TV in the lineup with QD-OLED technology; the new 2026 removes it.
articles.body:
The best gaming TV just dropped in price during eBay's annual Labor Day Sale. For a limited time, Electronic Express is offering the 65" Samsung S90F 4K OLED Smart TV for just $1,038.39 with free shipping when you apply 20% off coupon code " LABORDAY20 ". Electronic Express is an authorized Samsung reseller so you get a 1 year manufacturer's warranty. In one very important aspect (besides the price), the S90F is actually better than its S90H successor.

The 2025 Samsung S90F TV Is Better Than the 2026 S90H

The S90F is the 2025 model in Samsung's S90 OLED TV lineup. This is the last TV in the S90 series that's equipped with a quantum dot OLED panel. This year, Samsung decided to remove quantum dot technology from the S90 series, which means the only way to get a QD-OLED TV in 2026 is splurging for the S95H TV. The 65" S95H TV sells for $2,800 .

The S90F is equipped with Samsung's coveted quantum dot OLED panel which delivers a brighter picture and richer colors than W-OLED panels (like the one found in the S90H) while retaining all of the other benefits of OLED: near instaneous response time, true black levels, near infinite contrast ratio, and outstanding viewing angles. The Samsung S90F also has the features you'd want in a gaming TV , including a native 120Hz panel and HDMI 2.1 ports so you can run PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X games in 4K resolution at up to 120fps.

Despite being a current generation console, the Nintendo Switch 2 has lax TV requirements compared to the PS5 or Xbox Series X. When the Switch is connected to its dock and a television, it can only output a 4K resolution signal at up to 60 frames per second. That said, the Switch 2 will still benefit greatly from the OLED's stellar image quality.
